holding_summary: The court held that a surviving spouse's homestead right encompasses exclusive title to the rents and income from the homestead property -- here a 40-room rooming house that had served as the family's business homestead -- regardless of whether the property is rented out in whole or part or operated as the survivor's own business, and such income is not subject to partition among the heirs. The survivor was nonetheless treated as a life tenant, liable for ordinary current taxes but without a right to reimbursement for ordinary repairs from the remaindermen.

quotes.text: all revenues, rents, and income derived from the homestead, as such, are the separate and individual property of the survivor and that without any reference whatever to whether the same is rented out either in whole or in part by the survivor, or used by him in a business of his own

The court does not classify the roomer arrangements themselves as lease/license/lodging, so characterization is left null; duration of individual roomer occupancy is not stated in the facts.

Note-transfer/garnishment dispute and validity of a spendthrift trust devising a home to a beneficiary; property occupancy is incidental (a devised home the beneficiary was merely permitted to occupy), no compensated letting of rooms/dwellings at issue.
